name = "aspose-cells-foss-rust"

description = "Pure-Rust, open-source library to read and write Excel .xlsx workbooks with an Aspose.Cells-compatible API."

agent_guidance.content:
# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI coding agents working in this repository.

## Project overview

`aspose-cells-foss-rust` is a pure-Rust, MIT-licensed library that reads and writes Excel
`.xlsx` (OOXML / SpreadsheetML) workbooks. It exposes an API modeled after
[Aspose.Cells](https://products.aspose.com/cells/) - `Workbook` / `Worksheet` / `Cells` -
so the object model and method names intentionally mirror Aspose.Cells rather than typical
Rust idiom. **Preserve that naming when adding API surface** (`get_worksheets_mut()`,
`put_value_string()`, etc.); do not "rustify" public method names.

All OOXML packaging (ZIP container, relationships, shared strings, styles, worksheet XML,
charts) is implemented from scratch. The package name is `aspose-cells-foss-rust`; the
library is imported as `aspose_cells_foss_rust`.

## Commands

```bash
cargo build                    # build the library
cargo check --all-targets      # fast type-check, including samples
cargo fmt --all                # format (CI gates on `cargo fmt --all --check`)
cargo clippy --all-targets     # lint
cargo test --all-targets       # see "Testing" below
cargo run --bin sample_basic   # run a sample; writes to output/samples/
cargo build --bins             # build all sample binaries
cargo doc --no-deps            # build rustdoc locally
```

CI ([`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml)) runs fmt, check, clippy, test,
sample smoke tests, and bench on Linux x64, Windows x64, macOS ARM (`macos-14`), and
macOS x64 (`macos-13`). Run `cargo fmt --all` before finishing any change; the fmt gate is
enforced.

API docs are published by GitHub Pages through
[`pages.yml`](.github/workflows/pages.yml). The workflow generates rustdoc from
`cargo doc --no-deps` and deploys it when the repository Pages source is set to
`GitHub Actions`.

## Architecture

### Module wiring - read this before adding files

This repo does **not** use conventional Rust module layout. Files are `PascalCase.rs`
(matching the type they define), live in `src/Aspose.Cells_FOSS/`, and are wired together
by explicit `#[path]` attributes in `src/Aspose.Cells_FOSS/api.rs`. There are no `mod.rs`
files.

`src/lib.rs` declares one module and re-exports the public API:

```rust
#[path = "Aspose.Cells_FOSS/api.rs"]
mod api;
pub use api::{ Workbook, Worksheet, Cell, /* ... */ };
```

`api.rs` in turn wires every type:

```rust
#[path = "Chart.rs"]
mod chart;
pub use chart::Chart;
```

Individual modules glob-import their siblings via `use super::*;`, so within a module,
every other type is already in scope without an explicit import.

**To add a new public type**, all three steps are required:
1. Create `src/Aspose.Cells_FOSS/YourType.rs`, starting with `use super::*;`
2. Add `#[path = "YourType.rs"] mod your_type; pub use your_type::YourType;` to `api.rs`
3. Add `YourType` to the `pub use api::{...}` list in `src/lib.rs`

Skipping step 3 leaves the type invisible to library consumers.

### Layer layout

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/lib.rs` | Crate root; public re-exports and a crate-wide `clippy::allow` list |
| `Aspose.Cells_FOSS/api.rs` | Module wiring hub; defines `CellsError` and shared types |
| `Aspose.Cells_FOSS/*.rs` | Public facade types (`Workbook`, `Chart`, `Cell`, ...) |
| `Aspose.Cells_FOSS/*Live.rs` | Internal `pub(crate)` data structs backing the facades (for example `ChartData`) |
| `Aspose.Cells_FOSS/Core/` | Internal data models (`*Model.rs`) and value types |
| `Aspose.Cells_FOSS/Packaging/` | OOXML package (ZIP) reading/writing, relationships |
| `Aspose.Cells_FOSS/Xml/` | SpreadsheetML XML mappers |
| `Aspose.Cells_FOSS/Validation/` | Workbook validation |
| `Aspose.Cells_FOSS/Xlsx*.rs` | Serializer/loader per feature area (comments, pictures, styles, ...) |
| `Aspose.Cells_FOSS/ChartDefaults/` | XML templates pulled in via `include_str!` |
| `samples/` | Runnable examples, one `[[bin]]` per feature area |

### Facade pattern and `unsafe`

Public collection accessors return short-lived facade structs that hold a raw pointer to
an owner collection plus `PhantomData` for the lifetime:

```rust
pub struct Chart<'a> {
    pub(crate) owner: *mut Vec<ChartData>,
    pub(crate) index: usize,
    pub(crate) _marker: PhantomData<&'a mut Vec<ChartData>>,
}
```

This exists to reproduce the Aspose.Cells call style in Rust. Such files start with
`#![allow(unsafe_code)]` and each dereference carries a `// SAFETY:` comment. When touching
these, keep the `SAFETY` comments accurate and make sure a facade can never outlive its
owner.

### Error handling

`CellsError` (in `api.rs`) is the internal error enum - variants include
`SheetNotFound`, `InvalidCellReference`, `Io(String)`, and `Unsupported(&'static str)`.
Public API methods return `Result<_, _>`; propagate with `?` rather than panicking. Note
that many load paths collapse failures into `Unsupported("xlsx load")`, which discards
detail; prefer a more specific variant when adding new code.

## Conventions

- **Filenames** are `PascalCase.rs` and match the primary type; module names in `#[path]`
  declarations are `snake_case`.
- **Public API naming** mirrors Aspose.Cells (getter/setter style: `get_name()` /
  `set_name()`), not Rust convention.
- **Imports**: modules use `use super::*;`; do not add redundant sibling imports.
- **Formatting**: rustfmt defaults; run `cargo fmt --all`.
- **Clippy**: `src/lib.rs` carries a long crate-wide allow list (`too_many_lines`,
  `cast_possible_truncation`, etc.). Do not add new `allow`s to individual files without
  reason; prefer fixing the lint. CI does not use `-D warnings`, so warnings will not fail
  the build, but do not add new ones.

## Testing

**The repository currently has no unit/integration tests** (`cargo test --all-targets`
reports 0 tests). There is no `tests/` directory and no benchmarks with assertions -
`cargo bench` compiles but runs nothing.

Because of this, the **samples are the de-facto verification suite**. After a change that
touches the read/write path, run the relevant sample and confirm it still round-trips:

```bash
cargo run --bin sample_basic
cargo run --bin sample_loading
cargo run --bin sample_styles
```

The CI workflow already smoke-tests those three samples on Linux. If you touch charts,
pictures, comments, tables, or another specialized area, also run the nearest feature
sample manually.

Each sample creates a workbook, saves it to `output/samples/`, then loads it back and
prints what it read. If you add tests that depend on fixture workbooks, commit the fixture;
a prior test was removed because it referenced an `Input/roundtrip/*.xlsx` file that was
never committed, so it failed everywhere.

## Dependencies

Pinned deliberately; check before bumping:

| Crate | Version | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `zip` | 0.6 | **Pinned to 0.6.** The code uses the non-generic `FileOptions::default()`; zip 2.x made `FileOptions` generic and will not compile as written. |
| `roxmltree` | 0.20 | XML parsing on load; used via full paths (`roxmltree::Document::parse`) |
| `chrono` | 0.4 | date/time cell values |
| `sha2`, `base64`, `getrandom` | 0.10 / 0.22 / 0.3 | workbook protection hashing; `getrandom::fill` is the 0.3 API |
| `serde_json` | 1 | value formatting helpers |

There is no `rust-toolchain.toml`; CI uses stable. Edition 2021.

## Gotchas

- Do not restructure the `#[path]` module wiring into conventional Rust modules; the whole
  tree depends on it.
- Adding a public type requires editing **both** `api.rs` and `lib.rs`.
- `output/` and `target/` are gitignored; samples write into `output/samples/`.
- The repository keeps the license text in both [LICENSE.txt](LICENSE.txt) and
  [License/LICENSE.txt](License/LICENSE.txt). Prefer the root `LICENSE.txt` when linking
  from repo-facing documentation.
